solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Holst worried nervously before opening of his — such as Planets?

indicators.note: done nervously, things are jittery and jumbled, so the preceding words get shaken into a new order

parts.note: both words taken as written, as letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of his

explanation.surface: Gustav Holst frets over how his suite The Planets will open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters; 'nervously' does the mixing. Holst's The Planets suite makes the definition apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Things like the planets in Holst's suite are unearthly and remote, belonging to another world, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Foul-mouthed one maybe bringing up rumour with nothing in it

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up lifts it from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards
having something in it means the zero is placed inside the other word

parts.note: a report is a piece of hearsay or rumour
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone with a filthy tongue spreads gossip that has no substance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'swear like a trooper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry soldier is proverbially coarse in speech, as in the idiom swearing like one, so he is an example of a foul-mouthed person.

clue.text: One panting for the psalmodist in the spirit of Spenser?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Psalm 42 opens 'As the ... panteth after the water brooks'
second meaning: Spenser's spelling of heart, the seat of spirit and feeling

explanation.walkthrough: The psalmist's deer panting for water is Psalm 42; Spenser, the Elizabethan poet, spelt heart this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A male red deer is the creature in the Psalm; and the same spelling is Spenser's archaic form of the word for the heart or spirit.

clue.text: Long-distance race that requires energy staggering round

indicators.note: something staggering lurches about unsteadily, so the word beside it is reeled into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
round, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gruelling long-distance race demands energy from runners staggering around the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a lap of the race but is the word to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for an endurance contest, typically for motorcycles or bikes over rough ground, run over a long distance.

clue.text: Pull up, dear –'ow yer doin'?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: to tow is to pull
French for dear

explanation.surface: A Cockney greets a friend who has just pulled up: hello, love, how are you?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' reads like a car stopping, but 'up' turns the pulling word round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Cockney or slangy British greeting, the equivalent of the dropped-aitch 'how are you doing?'.

clue.text: In aforesaid work father ransacked attic, opening love letters? (11, two words)

indicators.note: the father and the attic go in by opening up the pair of letters, which then sit on either side

parts.note: love is O, nil in tennis, so two of them make the letters
French for father

indicators.note: a ransacked room has everything turned over and out of place, so the word is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to rearrange

explanation.surface: In a book already cited, a father searches the attic and opens old love letters.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERE CITATO is Latin, abbreviated op. cit. in footnotes; 'love letters' are just two Os, not billets-doux.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in references to point back to a work already quoted, literally 'in the work cited'.

clue.text: Linked climbing party, thorough, outer pair removed

indicators.note: the outer pair are a word's first and last letters, and these are taken away

parts.note: proper as in 'a proper mess', thorough

explanation.surface: A thorough mountaineering team roped together, minus its two end climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: In mountaineering, a party linked by a line is itself called a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers tied together on one line are called a rope, so a linked climbing team is a technical sense of the word.

clue.text: A hound's tail wagging with the hunt's climax

indicators.note: a wagging thing moves to and fro, so these letters get swung into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word's tail is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of hound
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hound wags its tail as the hunt reaches its peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'the' belongs to both the letters and the definition's phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox hunt culminates in the kill of the quarry, traditionally called being 'in at the death'.

clue.text: I'm up on almost everything relating to flower family

indicators.note: almost the whole word means stopping one letter short of its end

parts.note: 'I'm up' as in mounted on a horse: I ride
everything is all

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being on top of nearly everything about a flowering plant family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm up' means I'm in the saddle, so I ride.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the Iridaceae, the iris family of plants, as a botanical term.

clue.text: Cutting short a shirt in the Scottish style

definitions.text: a shirt in the Scottish style

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: sarky is British slang for sarcastic, cutting

explanation.surface: A tailor trims a shirt in a Scottish fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' seems to be a tailoring term, but it means sharp-tongued; SARKY is British slang for sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect a shirt or chemise is called by this word, hence a Scottish-style shirt.

clue.text: Stacks of discs, good, with Prince on

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a rana is a Rajput prince, placed on after the first letter

explanation.surface: Piles of records, good ones, playing with Prince on the turntable.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince seems to be the pop star on a disc; it is RANA, an Indian prince.
explanation.definitionFit: In a chloroplast, the stacked membrane discs called thylakoids form structures known by this plural botanical term.

clue.text: Colonel in cavalry regiment, familiar in G & S whimsy

indicators.note: in places the word for familiar inside the pair of letters around it

parts.note: the two letters, joined by the ampersand
old as in 'good old Joe', familiar
a tick in the sense of a whim or caprice

explanation.surface: A cavalry colonel shows up in some whimsical Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: G & S suggests Gilbert and Sullivan, but it is just the letters G and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial title is borne by the colonels of the Household Cavalry regiments, the Life Guards and Blues and Royals, who carry a gilded staff.

clue.text: Wherein you'll see houris are dancing, with time off?

definitions.text: Wherein you'll see houris are dancing, with time off
definitions.note: the whole clue describes a seraglio, where maidens dance at leisure

indicators.note: dancing letters move around, so they end up in a fresh order
off means a unit of time is taken out of the letters

parts.note: both words taken as written
an hour is a measure of time, here removed

explanation.surface: A harem where beautiful maidens dance, with time off for rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houris' does double duty: the definition's picture and the source of letters. Houris are beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Turkish palace or seraglio, the place that housed a harem, so it is where such maidens would be found.

clue.text: During visit takes in odd features of Natal at once

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the selected letters go into the visit word

parts.note: a stay is a visit

indicators.note: odd features are the letters in odd-numbered places: first, third, fifth

parts.note: letters 1, 3 and 5 of Natal

explanation.surface: A visit to Natal, in South Africa, takes in its odd sights straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, without any delay: an adverb synonym.

clue.text: Nae one's ain gyte? Lead on one's held by t' reins, cruelly

indicators.note: being held by something means sitting inside it
treated cruelly, the letters are knocked about and jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to rearrange
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a is one, and 'on' places it after the lead symbol

explanation.surface: A Scot asks whose brat this is, as a child on leading reins is cruelly held.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in Scots: 'nae' is not, 'ain' is own, and a gyte is a child, so it means 'not one's own child?'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a bairn is a child, and a step-bairn is a stepchild, someone's child who is not their own offspring.

clue.text: Place for used cars, American? One wouldn't be seen there

definitions.note: a cryptic hint: the answer is something unlikely to be found on such a lot

parts.note: a car lot is where used cars are sold
abbreviation for United States, American

explanation.surface: An American used-car lot, where a certain sort of car would never appear.
explanation.walkthrough: Lotus is a British sports car maker, a car unlikely to turn up on an American used-car lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lotus is a British sports car, the 'one' that the clue jokes would never be seen on a US forecourt.

clue.text: Prop, second sent off — team was cock-a-hoop

indicators.note: a player sent off leaves the field, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a screw is a ship's propeller, a prop
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A rugby prop forward is sent off, and the opposing team crowed with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prop' suggests a rugby forward but means a propeller; the clue then gives two meanings of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a working team; and to crow, past tense crew, is to exult boastfully, being cock-a-hoop.

clue.text: Shave bit off fitness regime after start of exercises?

indicators.note: with a bit off, the word loses a letter from its end
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of exercises
Pilates is a popular exercise system

explanation.surface: Shaving a bit off as part of a fitness routine before the exercise starts.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove hair from the body, as shaving does, is the dictionary sense of this verb.

clue.text: Wearing old headcloth, one's tense beside costly French cook

parts.note: French for expensive
a chef is a cook
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense; 'beside' places it next to the rest

explanation.surface: A tense chef sits beside an expensive French cook, wearing a head scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' means the answer is the tense letter placed beside the French word and the cook.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adjective means kerchiefed, covered with a kerchief, an old type of headcloth.

clue.text: His is wake-up call, old, in duty list?

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for old inside the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties
O is an abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the early wake-up call is on the old duty rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wake-up call' suggests a hotel rota, but the definition is the bird whose crow is the dawn alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel crows at dawn, so his cry is the traditional farmyard alarm that wakes people up.

clue.text: One of many in orchard: true fir? Wrong

indicators.note: if the letters are wrong they need to be put right by rearranging them

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: Is this orchard tree a true fir? No, it is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruiter is a tree that bears fruit, so it is one of the many trees planted in an orchard.

clue.text: Foreign soldier heading off short-sighted ones retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the letters run the other way
with its heading off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: myopes are people who are short-sighted

explanation.surface: A soldier abroad marches off ahead of a group of short-sighted troops falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepoy was an Indian soldier serving under British or other European command, hence a foreign soldier.

clue.text: Sort of salmon active in freshwater algae

parts.note: the char is a fish of the salmon family
A is the abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: A kind of salmon swims actively among the algae of a freshwater lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the wordplay to the definition rather than putting one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Chara is a genus of stoneworts, green algae found in fresh water, used as a collective name.

clue.text: Pages replacing bishop in cheer for wedding ceremony

indicators.note: replacing means one set of letters takes the place of another

parts.note: a hurrah is a cheer
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title, which comes out
pp is the abbreviation for pages, which go in

explanation.surface: Page boys stand in for the bishop amid cheering at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: RR is Right Reverend, the style of a bishop. A huppah is the canopy of a Jewish wedding, and by extension the ceremony itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish tradition the marriage takes place under a canopy, and the word names both the canopy and the wedding service.

clue.text: Church candle in middle of holiday rector lit

indicators.note: lit means drunk, and drunken letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the middle of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter

parts.note: the central letter of holiday
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rector lights a church candle midway through a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit' suggests lighting the candle but means drunk, so it mixes the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricerion is a three-branched candlestick used by a bishop in Eastern Orthodox services, so a church candle.

clue.text: Short vestment, excessive one with cape on top

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape, placed on top in a down entry
OTT, over the top, is excessive
a means one

explanation.surface: A short church vestment is excessive when it comes with a cape over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a garment beside the vestment but is just a headland, C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short surplice worn by choristers and clergy, so it is a brief liturgical garment.

clue.text: Chemical once used by e.g. 20 scare curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an alarm is a scare

explanation.surface: A chemical once sprayed by apple growers caused a food scare and was cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to FRUITER at 20 down, a fruit tree; Alar was a growth regulator sprayed on apples until a 1989 health scare.
explanation.definitionFit: Alar is the trade name for daminozide, sprayed on fruit trees, notably apples, before it was withdrawn.

clue.text: Start of bidding resting with south? More than one club's crazy

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: first letter of bidding
at as in located with, resting at
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: At bridge, the bidding rests with South: is more than one club bid crazy?
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge picture misleads: clubs are cricket or baseball bats, and 'club's' stands for 'clubs are'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats are clubs used to hit a ball, so plural clubs; and bats is also informal for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Like distinctive woollies, knitted angora — bargain struck

indicators.note: knitting works yarn into a new pattern, so these letters are reworked into another order
struck as in struck off or struck out: removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
a go is a bargain or deal, as in 'it's a go'

explanation.surface: Distinctive jumpers knitted from angora wool, a bargain struck.
explanation.walkthrough: Aran sweaters, cable-knit jumpers from the Aran Islands of Ireland, are the woollies.
explanation.definitionFit: Aran is the name of a thick cable-pattern knitting style from the Irish islands, used as an adjective for such garments.

clue.text: Something to extend sail, right in light rainfall

indicators.note: in places the letter for right inside the word for drizzle

parts.note: to spit is to rain lightly
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sailor checks the rigging that spreads a sail, out in the drizzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprit is a spar running diagonally across a fore-and-aft sail to stretch it out.

clue.text: Work on English for Finnish song

parts.note: to run something is to work it, as in run a machine
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Working on an English version of a Finnish song.
explanation.walkthrough: A rune here is not a letter of an alphabet but a canto of Finnish epic verse, such as the Kalevala.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalevala and other Finnish poetry are made up of sung sections called runes, a specialist sense of the word.

clue.text: Box lined with wooden strip, lattice-like

indicators.note: something lined with a material has it on its inside, so the strip goes inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a box
a lath is a thin strip of wood

explanation.surface: A box lined with wooden slats looks like latticework.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a structure resembling trellis-work, used in botany and chemistry for cage-like forms.

clue.text: Food that's dry inside, about 500g in China

indicators.note: inside means the word for dry sits within the word for food

parts.note: kai is a New Zealand word for food
TT, teetotal, means dry, not drinking

explanation.surface: Food that is dry inside weighs about half a kilo in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means abstaining from alcohol, hence TT for teetotal; KAI is Maori and New Zealand English for food.
explanation.definitionFit: The katti, or catty, is a traditional Chinese and East Asian unit of weight of roughly a pound and a third.

clue.text: Not old, captivated by fashion on the decline

indicators.note: being captivated by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a fashion or manner is a way of doing something
ne is an archaic word for not

explanation.surface: Something modern, swept up by fashion, now going out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not old' looks like new; it means the old word for not, NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Waney means waning, decreasing, which is what something on the decline is doing.

clue.text: Train company, ailing, got there and ran with reduced service? (13, two words)

indicators.note: something ailing is out of sorts, so these letters are out of order and need sorting

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Royal Navy, the senior service, reduced to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: An unwell rail operator arrived late and ran a cut-back timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced service' sounds like rail cuts but is RN, the Royal Navy, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Northern is the name of a British railway operator, historically the Great Northern Railway, now a train franchise brand.
